clue.text: Crabby priest accepts holy orders at first

indicators.note: a word that accepts something takes it in, so the priest's word holds the other letters

parts.note: a cleric is a priest or other churchman

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered clergyman takes on the duties of holy orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crabby' sounds like a mood but is the definition; 'holy orders' tempts as the church's sacrament, yet only its two initials are used, held by the word 'accepts' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Choleric means irritable and quick to anger, so a crabby person has this temperament.

clue.text: Jerkin and grey 'eadgear viewed from behind

indicators.note: seeing something from behind shows it the other way round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: drab is a dull greyish-brown colour
'eadgear is headgear with the H dropped, Cockney style, so hat loses its H

explanation.surface: A sleeveless jacket and a grey Cockney hat are seen from the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'eadgear tells you to drop the H from the hat as well; 'viewed from behind' then turns the whole run round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a short sleeveless tunic, a type of jerkin worn over armour or as a herald's coat.

clue.text: What did you say about old man retiring? That's brave!

indicators.note: something retiring draws back, so the whole string of letters is read backwards

parts.note: eh? is the questioning sound made when you have not heard someone
ca, short for circa, means about
pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a remark about a man's retirement to be repeated, then praises his courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns the whole run EH + CA + PA backwards. 'That's' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, and the Apache are one such people, so the answer is an example.

clue.text: Part of Titanic perhaps revived in dark empty cinema

indicators.note: something revived is brought back in new form, so the letters are rearranged
an empty word has lost its inside letters, leaving only its first and last

explanation.surface: A scene from the film Titanic is shown again in a dark, deserted picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves DK from 'dark'; 'revived' rearranges DK with CINEMA. The film's success makes Titanic look like the movie, but it is the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A main deck is the principal deck of a ship, so the liner Titanic had one as an example.

clue.text: Disturbance in Scottish city suffering fish shortage

indicators.note: a shortage of something means it is missing, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Stirling is a city in central Scotland
the ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A commotion breaks out in a Scottish city when it runs short of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortage' with 'suffering' takes LING out of STIRLING.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a commotion or fuss, a common synonym for a public disturbance.

clue.text: Approaching road junction

definitions.meaning: ... means approximately, nearly reaching a figure, as in ... fifty
a circular junction where traffic flows one way round a central island

explanation.walkthrough: A roundabout is the circular road junction found all over Britain, where Americans would have a traffic circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase round about means nearly, and the word also names a circular traffic junction common in Britain.

clue.text: Lengthen treatise begun by expert

indicators.note: begun by puts the second piece at the front, so the expert's word comes first

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
a tract is a short written treatise or pamphlet

explanation.surface: A specialist starts writing a long essay that will run on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract is to prolong or draw out, so it means to lengthen in time.

clue.text: Heads off towards Rome in package tour

indicators.note: the heads of the following words are their first letters, to be taken off and used

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers set out for Rome on a package holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads off' takes the first letters of 'towards Rome in package'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a journey or excursion, so it can stand for a tour.

clue.text: Card game old servicemen rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters run in reverse order

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is made up of servicemen

explanation.surface: Old soldiers turn down the offer of a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns O + RAF round. The RAF is Britain's air force.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is an old gambling card game in which players bet on the order of cards drawn from a box.

clue.text: Held in place, it can trap fish

definitions.text: Held in place, it can trap fish

parts.words: Held in place, it can trap fish
parts.note: describes a fishing net fixed by posts driven into a river bed or shore so it stays put to catch fish

explanation.surface: Something kept fixed in position is able to catch fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The posts that hold this net up are what give it the first part of its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishing net stretched on posts fixed in the water bed, staying in place to catch passing fish.

clue.text: Thought Tory team left of centre?

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for a Conservative, a Tory
a side is a sports team
red is the colour of the political left; the question mark admits this is loose

explanation.surface: A political commentator wonders whether the Conservative team has drifted leftwards.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics the Tories are the Conservatives (CON), and RED stands for left-wing politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Considered, as in a considered view, means thought about carefully, so the two words share a sense.

clue.text: A journey without end lacking interest

indicators.note: without end means the final letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a ride is a journey on horseback or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: An endless journey can be dreadfully dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without end' drops the E from RIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid in its figurative sense describes something dry and dull, so lacking interest.

clue.text: Dish of meat cut near oven, and temperature checked

indicators.note: a cut word loses its end, here the final letter
checked means held in, so the letter for temperature is held inside the shortened word

parts.note: near means left, as on the near side of a horse, and port is the left side of a ship
an oast is a kiln or oven for drying hops

explanation.surface: A cook prepares a joint, sets it by the oven and keeps checking the temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of the left-hand side to give POR; 'checked' holds the temperature letter inside, giving POTR. Oast houses are the hop-drying kilns of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot roast is a joint of meat browned and then cooked slowly in a covered pot, so it is a dish of meat.

clue.text: Musical opus starting with organ accompaniment

indicators.note: starting with puts the first piece at the start, followed by the second

parts.note: op. or O is used for opus, a numbered musical work
the liver is an organ of the body

explanation.surface: A musical work begins with an organ playing along.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a church organ; the organ is the liver. 'accompaniment' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionel Bart's show based on Dickens's Oliver Twist is a famous stage musical.

clue.text: Remained remarkably steady (and sounds it)

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something strange has happened to the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stayed calm and steady, and their very name sounds steady too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkably' rearranges STEADY. The bracket adds that the answer, said out loud, also sounds like staid, meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Stayed is the past tense of stay, so it means remained in place.

clue.text: Compassion shown by hospital, one nursing old lady

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: unity is oneness, the number one
ma is an informal word for mother, one's old lady

explanation.surface: A hospital shows kindness when someone looks after an elderly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing' holds the old lady inside oneness. 'One' looks like the usual I, but here it is the whole idea of oneness.
explanation.definitionFit: Humanity can mean kindness and benevolence toward others, so it is a synonym for compassion.

clue.text: Shift work accepted during strike

indicators.note: something accepted during another word sits inside it

parts.note: to hit is to strike
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Moving to a different shift pattern is agreed in the middle of industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted during' sets the work inside the blow. 'Shift' looks like a work rota but is the order to move off; 'strike' looks like industrial action but means a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Hop it is a British slang order to go away, so it means shift in the sense of move yourself.

clue.text: Injuries of one creature seized by wild cats

indicators.note: something seized by another is held inside it

parts.note: lions are big wild cats
an ace is the one in a pack of cards
a rat is a creature

explanation.surface: Someone describes the wounds suffered by an animal caught by wild cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seized by' holds the card's one and the rodent inside the big cats. 'wild' tempts as an anagram signal, but 'wild cats' is a single idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerations are deep cuts or tears in the skin, a kind of injury.

clue.text: Largely willing to consume the old British bakery product

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so the shortened word swallows the other letters
largely means mostly, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: ready means willing, as in ready to help
ye is an old form of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe

explanation.surface: Someone is mostly happy to eat the traditional British loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' trims the last letter from the willing word, leaving READ; 'to consume' then swallows the old article and the British abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye bread is bread made from rye flour, sold in bakeries, so it is a bakery product.

clue.text: Prove fit to score, cup match being rearranged

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A team has to show it is ready to win when a cup tie is moved to a new date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being rearranged' reorders the letters of TO SCORE CUP MATCH. The surface makes it sound like a fixture being moved.
explanation.definitionFit: To come up to scratch is an idiom for reaching the required standard, so to prove fit for something.

clue.text: After sound of shot, notices groups of criminals

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first
sound of means the word is heard, not seen, so letters that sound the same are used

parts.note: a try is a shot or attempt, as in have a shot at it
ads, advertisements, are notices

explanation.surface: Following the noise of gunfire, police see notices about criminal gangs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like gunfire but means an attempt, a TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Triads are Chinese secret societies running organised crime, so they are groups of criminals.

clue.text: Person giving some basic personal information up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: DOB, date of birth, is a basic piece of personal information on any form

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a few basic details about themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DOB round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Bod is British slang for a person, as in an odd bod.

clue.text: Park, as it happens, keeps us apart from others

parts.note: a rec, a recreation ground, is a public park

indicators.note: a word that keeps another holds it inside

parts.note: live describes a broadcast going out as it happens
taken as written

explanation.surface: A park, as it turns out, keeps us away from other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' holds the pronoun inside the broadcast word. A rec is the British name for a local recreation ground; 'as it happens' looks like a link phrase but is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A reclusive person lives withdrawn from society, so they keep apart from others.

clue.text: Curses old boy going over the limit

indicators.note: going over means turning over, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
taken as written
a ration is a fixed limit on how much one may have

explanation.surface: A former pupil swears after exceeding his allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' flips the old boy to BO. 'over the limit' reads as a drink-driving phrase, but the words split between indicator and pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Botheration is a mild exclamation of annoyance, used just like the oath Curses!

clue.text: Use logic, when working to infiltrate soldiers abroad

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so these letters go between the others

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers in the British Army
out can mean abroad, away from home
as means when, as in as he arrived
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Someone thinks hard about how to get inside an army unit overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to infiltrate' slips the two small words for when and working between the army unit and the word for abroad. The Royal Engineers are a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason out is to work something through by logical thought, so to use logic.

clue.text: Creature man destroyed with sword

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A monster is killed by a man with a sword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges MAN and SWORD; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandworm is a marine worm that burrows in sand, and so it is a creature.

clue.text: King needing tips to end conflict with duke

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, first and last letters

parts.note: war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A monarch needs advice on ending a war, along with a duke's support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips to' takes ED, the outside letters of 'end'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward is the name of several English kings, so the answer is an example of a king.

clue.text: Austrian musician, not good, eclipsed by Italian composer

indicators.note: something eclipsed by another is covered by it, so it goes inside
not tells you to take away the letter for good

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School

explanation.surface: An Austrian musician, being no good, is outshone by an Italian composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the good letter from the Austrian to leave BER; 'eclipsed by' sets it inside the Italian abbreviation. 'Italian composer' reads as one phrase, but the definition is only 'composer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Ibert was a twentieth-century French composer, so the answer is an example of a composer.

clue.text: Swimmer's blue, but not cold

indicators.note: not means the letter for cold is taken away

parts.note: blue means risque or indecent, as is racy
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A swimmer looks blue, though apparently not from the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like a colour or low mood, but means saucy, RACY.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray is a flat fish with wing-like fins, so it is a swimmer.
